chapterNote: The book's prologue (vv. 1-7) states its purpose: wisdom, discipline, and understanding — with the fear of the LORD as the first principle. Then two voices contend for the son: the enticer's voice calling him into a gang of robbers (vv. 8-19) and Wisdom's voice crying aloud in the public square (vv. 20-33). The chapter sets up the whole book's drama — which voice will the son obey?

1.text: These are the proverbs of Solomon, the son of David, who reigned as king over Israel:
1.amp: These are the proverbs [mashal — pithy comparisons, sayings that set one thing alongside another to teach] of Solomon, the son of David, who reigned as king over Israel.
1.notes: mashal (H4912) = a proverb, parable, byword — literally a 'comparison'; the whole book operates by setting two ways, two ends, two voices alongside each other.

2.text: to know wisdom and discipline, to discern words of true understanding,
2.amp: to know wisdom [chokmah — skill in living, not bookish information] and discipline [musar — corrective instruction, sometimes painful], to discern words of true understanding [binah — the trained ability to tell one thing from another].
2.notes: chokmah (H2451), musar (H4148), and binah (H998) are the prologue's three pillars; chokmah is practical skill at the art of life, musar is the formative correction that shapes it, binah is the eye that distinguishes wise from foolish in real time.

3.text: to receive the discipline that gives prudent skill — righteousness, justice, and straight dealing —
3.amp: to receive the discipline that gives prudent skill [haskel — the kind of insight that produces good outcomes], righteousness [tsedeq — right relating], justice [mishpat — right deciding], and straight dealing [meysharim — honest, level conduct].
3.notes: haskel (H7919) = to act with skill/success; tsedeq (H6664) = righteousness; mishpat (H4941) = justice/judgment; meysharim (H4339) = uprightness, things that are straight rather than crooked.

4.text: to give shrewdness to the simple and to the young man knowledge and the discretion to use it well.
4.amp: to give shrewdness [ormah — street-smart prudence, the same word for the serpent's craftiness in Gen 3 but here put to good use] to the simple [peti — the naive, easily-led], and to the young man knowledge and the discretion to use it well [mezimmah — the planning mind, which can serve good or evil depending on the heart].
4.notes: peti (H6612) = the open/naive one, susceptible to either voice; ormah (H6195) and mezimmah (H4209) are both 'gray' words — they describe sharp practical intelligence which is a virtue when ruled by the fear of the LORD and a vice without it.

5.text: Let the wise man hear and grow in his learning, and the man of understanding gain wise guidance —
5.amp: Let the wise man hear and grow in his learning [lekach — what he takes in], and the man of understanding gain wise guidance [tachbulah — literally 'steerings,' the sailor's image of pulling the ropes that turn a ship].
5.notes: lekach (H3948) = what one takes/learns; tachbulah (H8458) is from a root meaning 'rope/cable' — the wisdom that handles the steering lines of life. Proverbs assumes the wise still need to grow.

6.text: to understand a proverb and a parable, the sayings of the wise and their riddles.
6.amp: to understand a proverb [mashal] and a parable [melitsah — a saying with an enigma in it, requiring interpretation], the sayings of the wise and their riddles [chidah — the riddle that hides its meaning until you ponder it].
6.notes: melitsah (H4426) = a figure/satire; chidah (H2420) = a riddle (cf. Samson's riddle, Judg 14). Wisdom requires patience to unpack what is folded inside the saying.

7.text: Reverent fear of the LORD is the very first thing of true knowledge; fools, for their part, hold wisdom and discipline in contempt.
7.amp: Reverent fear of the LORD [yirat YHWH — trembling awe, the right posture before the holy God] is the very first thing of true knowledge [reshith — the head and starting-point]; fools, for their part, hold wisdom and discipline in contempt [treating correction as an insult rather than a gift].
7.notes: yirat YHWH (H3374 + H3068) = the fear of the LORD — the book's master theme; reshith (H7225) = beginning, both 'first in time' and 'first in importance.' Without this fear, knowledge has no foundation; with it, knowledge has a Center.

8.text: Hear, my son, your father's discipline, and do not forsake the teaching of your mother.
8.amp: Hear, my son, your father's discipline [musar — the correction shaped by long love], and do not forsake the teaching [torah — the instruction, the same word as 'Law'] of your mother.
8.notes: torah (H8451) in a domestic setting = the mother's instruction, which the son is to keep with the same reverence due to the Law itself. Solomon assumes godly parents and warns the son to honor both.

9.text: For they will be a graceful garland on your head and chains of honor about your neck.
9.amp: For they will be a graceful garland on your head [livyah chen — the wreath of favor, the kind a king or honored guest would wear] and chains of honor about your neck [the gold collar of distinction, not the chain of a captive but the ornament of a son in good standing].
9.notes: livyah chen (H3880 + H2580) = a wreath/garland of grace; the imagery is of public honor that a son's faithfulness to his parents' teaching visibly displays.

10.text: My son, if sinners try to entice you, do not consent.
10.amp: My son, if sinners try to entice you [pathah — to seduce, to draw open with persuasion], do not consent [aval — do not yield, do not say yes].
10.notes: pathah (H6601) = to seduce/persuade open — the same word for being deceived; the temptation appeals to fellowship and gain, both real human goods misdirected toward evil.

11.text: If they say, 'Come along with us — let us lie in ambush for blood, let us crouch in hiding for the harmless man, attacking him for no reason at all;
11.amp: If they say, 'Come along with us, let us lie in ambush for blood [arav — crouch in wait for the kill], let us crouch in hiding for the harmless man [naqi — the blameless, attacking him for no reason at all (chinnam)];
11.notes: arav (H693) = to ambush; chinnam (H2600) = without cause/gratuitously. The gang's evil is not in self-defense or rivalry — it is predatory, aimed at the harmless for sheer plunder.

12.text: let us swallow them alive like Sheol, whole, like those who go down to the pit;
12.amp: let us swallow them alive like Sheol [bala — gulp them down whole; the grave itself never sated], whole, like those who go down to the pit [bor — the cistern of death, the dark hole from which no one returns].
12.notes: Sheol (H7585) personified as the insatiable mouth that swallows the living (cf. Isa 5:14); bor (H953) = pit/cistern, often the grave. The gang takes the very posture of Death itself toward their victims.

13.text: we will find all kinds of costly wealth; we will fill our houses with plunder;
13.amp: we will find all kinds of costly wealth [hon yaqar — riches of every price]; we will fill our houses with plunder [shalal — the spoils of violence, taken from those who cannot defend them].
13.notes: shalal (H7998) = spoil/booty — the language of war stripping the defeated, but here applied to highway robbery and murder.

14.text: throw in your lot with us; we will all share one common purse' —
14.amp: throw in your lot with us [the dice-roll of the gang's brotherhood, all-in together]; we will all share one common purse [kis — the bag of pooled spoils; what is theirs is ours]' —
14.notes: kis (H3599) = bag/purse. The bait is brotherhood and equal share, dressed up to look like loyalty — but it is loyalty to a thieving fellowship, the counterfeit of the wise community Proverbs commends.

15.text: my son, do not walk in their way; hold your foot back from their path.
15.amp: my son, do not walk in their way [derek — the road, the pattern of life that road carries]; hold your foot back from their path [nathiv — the well-worn trail, the rut their feet are cutting].
15.notes: derek (H1870) = way/road/pattern of life; nathiv (H5410) = path/track. Two near-synonyms, doubled for emphasis: don't even set foot where they walk.

16.text: Their feet, after all, go racing toward what is wicked, and to spill blood they cannot hurry fast enough.
16.amp: Their feet, after all, go racing toward what is wicked [the appetite outruns the deliberation; they sprint toward harm], and to spill blood [shaphak dam — to pour it out] they cannot hurry fast enough [mahar — in a rush, no second thoughts].
16.notes: mahar (H4116) = to hasten; shaphak (H8210) = to pour out, shed; cf. Isa 59:7, Rom 3:15. The mark of the wicked is not slow descent but eager sprint — they cannot wait to do harm.

17.text: Surely it is in vain that the net is spread before the eyes of any bird;
17.amp: Surely it is in vain that the net is spread before the eyes of any bird [no creature with sight will fly into a trap it can plainly see];
17.notes: A proverb interpreters debate: probably 'even a bird sees a baited trap and avoids it — yet these fools rush into their own ruin with eyes wide open.' The gang's evil is self-defeating, and they know it less than the bird does.

18.text: but these men lie in wait for their own blood; they ambush their own lives.
18.amp: but these men lie in wait for their own blood [the ambush they set comes back on them]; they ambush their own lives [nephesh — they trap their own souls in the very pit they dug for others].
18.notes: The hunter becomes the hunted. The violence of the ambush boomerangs on the ambushers; cf. Ps 7:15-16; 9:15-16. Sin is finally suicidal.

19.text: Such are the ways of all who are greedy for unjust gain; it takes away the life of those who get it.
19.amp: Such are the ways of all who are greedy for unjust gain [betsa — the cut of profit gotten by violence or fraud]; it takes away the life of those who get it [the very gain they grasp for kills them].
19.notes: betsa (H1215) = unjust gain / cut — profit pursued at any cost; cf. 1 Tim 6:10. The verse names the master sin behind the gang's invitation: greed that will pay any price — even its own life.

20.text: Wisdom calls aloud in the open street; in the public square she lifts her voice.
20.amp: Wisdom calls aloud [ranan — shouts with full voice, no hiding] in the open street [chuts — outside, in the public way]; in the public square [rechovoth — the broad places] she lifts her voice.
20.notes: Wisdom is personified as a woman publicly preaching — the opposite of the gang that whispers in dark corners. Her appeal is open, witnessed, and free; cf. Prov 8:1-3, 9:1-6, where the figure is developed further. The Christian tradition reads this voice as a foreshadowing of Christ, the eternal Wisdom of God (1 Cor 1:24, 30).

21.text: At the head of the noisy streets she calls out; at the entrances of the city gates she speaks her piece:
21.amp: At the head of the noisy streets she calls out [where the marketplace clamor is loudest, her voice still rises]; at the entrances of the city gates she speaks her piece [the gates being the public seat of judgment and civic life, where elders sat and decisions were made].
21.notes: The city gate (shaar, H8179) was the ancient courtroom and town hall combined — Wisdom preaches at the seat of public life, refusing to be a private hobby.

22.text: 'How long, you simple ones, will you love your simplicity? How long will mockers delight in their mockery, and fools hate knowledge?
22.amp: 'How long, you simple ones [pethaim — the naive, the easily-led], will you love your simplicity [pethi — being open to any persuasion, never settling on truth]? How long will mockers [lets — the scoffer who treats holy things with contempt] delight in their mockery, and fools [kesil — the thick-headed who refuse correction] hate knowledge?
22.notes: Three classes of unwise: peti (H6612), the open/naive; lets (H3917), the scornful mocker; kesil (H3684), the dull-witted fool. Wisdom names the precise condition of each before calling them out of it.

23.text: Turn at my reproof! Behold, I will pour out my Spirit upon you; I will make my words known to you.
23.amp: Turn [shub — turn back, repent] at my reproof [tokhechah — the searching correction]! Behold, I will pour out my Spirit [ruach — breath, wind, Spirit] upon you; I will make my words known to you.
23.notes: shub (H7725) is the repentance verb par excellence; tokhechah (H8433) = reproof/argument. The offer is stunning: Wisdom will pour out her ruach (H7307) on those who turn — foreshadowing the gospel pattern where repentance opens onto the Spirit (Acts 2:38).

24.text: Because I have called and you refused, I have stretched out my hand and no one paid attention,
24.amp: Because I have called and you refused [me'an — a flat, settled No], I have stretched out my hand [the open hand of invitation, held out so long the arm is tired] and no one paid attention,
24.notes: me'an (H3985) = to refuse outright. Wisdom's invitation has been long and patient; the refusal is not lack of opportunity but settled choice. The 'stretched-out hand' is the LORD's own gesture toward Israel (cf. Isa 65:2; Rom 10:21).

25.text: you ignored all my counsel and would have none of my reproof,
25.amp: you ignored all my counsel [paraq — you let it drop, brushed it aside] and would have none of my reproof,
25.notes: paraq (H6544) = to let go / let slip / dismiss. The refusal is total: not selective hearing but blanket rejection.

26.text: I also will laugh at your disaster; I will mock when terror overtakes you,
26.amp: I also will laugh at your disaster [id — the day of calamity that crashes in]; I will mock when terror overtakes you,
26.notes: id (H343) = calamity/disaster. The laughter is not cruel amusement but the inevitable reversal: the mocker is mocked, the scoffer is scorned, by the very wisdom they spurned (cf. Ps 2:4; Prov 3:34).

27.text: when your terror comes like a storm, and your disaster sweeps in like a whirlwind, when distress and anguish come upon you.
27.amp: when your terror comes like a storm [sha'avah — the rushing devastation], and your disaster sweeps in like a whirlwind [suphah — the cyclone, sudden and total], when distress [tsarah — the pressing tightness] and anguish [tsuqah — the choking squeeze] come upon you.
27.notes: Four words for catastrophe piled up (sha'avah H7722, suphah H5492, tsarah H6869, tsuqah H6695) — the warning's force matches the storm it describes.

28.text: Then they will cry out to me, and I will give them no answer; they will hunt for me at the break of day, but they will not find me,
28.amp: Then they will cry out to me, and I will give them no answer; they will hunt for me at the break of day [shachar — urgently, with daybreak desperation], but they will not find me,
28.notes: shachar (H7836) = to seek early/urgently — the verb for desperate, daybreak-search; the tragedy is that the late seekers find Wisdom gone, the door of opportunity shut. Cf. Luke 13:25.

29.text: because they had hated knowledge, and the reverent fear of the LORD they had refused to choose;
29.amp: because they had hated knowledge, and the reverent fear of the LORD [yirat YHWH] they had refused to choose [they spurned the master principle of v.7, and so cut off all hope of true knowing];
29.notes: The diagnosis: not failure to find Wisdom but refusal to fear the LORD. Without that posture, knowledge cannot land; with it, knowledge takes root.

30.text: they would have none of my counsel, and they despised all my reproof.
30.amp: they would have none of my counsel, and they despised all my reproof [na'ats — treated it as worthless, spat on the very thing offered for their good].
30.notes: na'ats (H5006) = to spurn/despise/treat with contempt — the strongest verb for rejection of God's word.

31.text: Therefore they will eat the fruit of their own way; they will be filled with their own schemes.
31.amp: Therefore they will eat the fruit of their own way [the harvest of the seed they sowed — self-chosen, self-grown, self-served]; they will be filled with their own schemes [moetsah — the counsels they preferred to mine, now their whole diet].
31.notes: Their punishment is precisely their choice: they wanted their way, they get their way, and their way kills them. moetsah (H4156) = counsel/plan — the very thing they preferred to Wisdom's counsel becomes their portion.

32.text: For the backsliding of the simple will kill them, and the careless ease of fools will destroy them;
32.amp: For the backsliding [meshubah — the turning-away that began the slide] of the simple will kill them, and the careless ease [shalvah — complacent, untroubled prosperity] of fools will destroy them;
32.notes: meshubah (H4878) = apostasy/turning-back; shalvah (H7962) = quiet, untroubled ease. Two opposite-looking fates that finish the same way: the panicked drift of the simple and the smug security of the fool both end in ruin.

33.text: but whoever listens to me will dwell securely and will be at ease, without dread of evil.'
33.amp: but whoever listens to me will dwell securely [shakan betach — settle in safety, the verb of God dwelling among His people] and will be at ease, without dread of evil [sha'anan — the deep, undisturbed quietness of the man who knows his foundation will hold].'
33.notes: shakan (H7931) = to dwell/settle, used of God's tabernacle presence; betach (H983) = secure; sha'anan (H7600) = quiet/at-ease. The same words used elsewhere for God's own dwelling and the rest He gives His people — Wisdom's promise is not mere safety but a settled life under God's near presence.
